verdict.rationale: GitHub's own docs confirm you can create fine-grained personal access tokens and grant each one a set of permissions that define which API resources it can reach. The REST API also reports which permissions an endpoint requires. However, the evidence never documents limiting a token to specific repositories or setting an expiry date. missing for 10: documentation of repository-level scoping, documentation of token expiry dates, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create fine-grained access tokens limited to specific repositories, permissions, and an expiry date

citations.quote: When you create a fine-grained personal access token, you grant it a set of permissions. Permissions define what resources the token can access via the API.
The header will tell you what permissions are required in order to access the endpoint.
